feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital communications, credible progression, and relevant technical depth. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing scope, leadership, and ownership of major digital platforms and operations.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms.  
- Strong alignment between summary, experience, and skills; the profile consistently supports a digital strategy/communications leadership brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily; consolidating them would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities. Several bullets describe what you led or supported, but fewer show measurable results, improvements, or business/mission impact.  
- Fix style and grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; maintain consistent comma usage in lists (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a clearer senior-level value proposition would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Lead with your senior positioning and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications systems for mission-driven organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter phrase like “multi-channel digital communications” to reduce clutter.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, platform modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflow design, stakeholder coordination, and advocacy-focused messaging. Translates complex technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content and scalable digital systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats “cross-channel/multi-channel,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” already covered in Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo role descriptions, so keep it concise here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/technical strengths will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, CV-aligned phrasing: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial systems & governance • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow automation & systems design • Advocacy & policy communications • Stakeholder coordination • Multimedia & live event production
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; change “Multi-channel communication” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger seniority and consistency.
- Consider swapping “Web & CMS administration” for “CMS modernization & web operations,” which better reflects recent, higher-impact work.
- If space allows, prioritize competencies most supported by recent roles: digital strategy, Drupal/web platforms, analytics, governance, and multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level and not repeat exact wording.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around 3–4 highest-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or named deliverables.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type + value: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with outcome-oriented ones: “Built,” “Launched,” “Streamlined,” “Led,” “Improved.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by refining CMS workflows, front-end implementation, troubleshooting, and cross-channel governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages, publishers, turnaround reduction, engagement lift, search success, or toolkit downloads.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics there.
- “Governance/workflows/analytics” repeats NACo language; emphasize what is new in this consulting role.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It will be stronger if the opening is tighter, bullets start with outcomes, and channel-management points avoid repeating earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Replace the overview with: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: add % improvements for traffic, engagement, production cost/time savings, reporting speed, stakeholder adoption, or publishing consistency.
- Tighten channel bullet: “Oversaw enterprise email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials” rather than listing platforms generically.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version at a more strategic/enterprise level.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older multimedia bullets; emphasize first-time infrastructure and organizational capacity gains.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging during a period of organizational growth.”
- Tighten bullets and start with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable/process impact if available: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes spanning communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” is vague and duplicates governance/workflow language in the Director role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the program, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership scope rather than repeating generic digital/content terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording tied to recent work:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization  
- Editorial governance & content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging  
- Audience strategy, storytelling & campaign planning
- Keep each line parallel in structure; avoid mixing nouns (“strategy”) with softer descriptors (“audience-focused”).
- Prefer “content operations” over “content planning” to better reflect systems/governance leadership shown in recent roles.
- If space allows, consider one stronger qualifier like “high-volume” or “multi-stakeholder” to reinforce scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already covered in Core Competencies; keep only if this section is shortened elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent web modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to capability-led phrasing, with the most current strengths first.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- AI-enabled search and structured content experiences
- Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery
- API integrations, workflow automation and Airtable-based systems
- If space allows, replace older/lower-priority platforms with stronger recent signals: “Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, API integrations, workflow automation.”
- Keep platform names selective; use this section to show scope, not repeat every tool.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” is largely duplicated in “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS.”
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also repeat content covered in “Technical + IT > Automation & Workflow Systems.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. For a topline skills section, emphasize strategic capability and decision-making impact over listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to leadership-level capability, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting infrastructure & performance optimization.”
- Tighten to 5–6 items: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider replacing “Microsoft Clarity” with a broader phrase like “behavioral analytics” unless Clarity is a hiring keyword.
- If space allows, add outcome-oriented wording: “dashboarding and KPI design for executive decision-making” or “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web performance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the full tool stack here if those tools are already listed in Technical + IT; keep this section more strategic.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and with the Technical + IT tools list. Make it more outcome-oriented and leadership-level to match the seniority of recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic task terms with scope/level language: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio buildout and operations,” “PTZ/multi-camera production systems.”
- Add strategic framing to reflect recent experience: “In-house studio leadership” or “Multimedia systems for advocacy and member communications.”
- Keep to 4–5 items and tighten phrasing; e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- PTZ and multi-camera production systems
- Studio buildout and operations
- Advocacy multimedia programming
- If you can support it elsewhere, hint at scale: “Recurring advocacy video series” or “high-volume event support.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is partly duplicated by Premiere Pro/Audition under Technical + IT.
- “Livestreaming” repeats Core Competencies; use broader phrasing or swap in a more distinctive strength.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” It should emphasize platform depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than read like a duplicate keyword list.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put **Drupal first** and add a brief qualifier to reflect the strongest, most recent platform experience from current and NACo roles.
- Standardize naming: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of just “Power Pages.”
- If space allows, consider grouping by strength: **Primary: Drupal | Working knowledge: WordPress, SharePoint, Microsoft Power Pages, GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this one more platform-specific.
- Avoid repeating CMS modernization here since it already appears in Topline Skills and work experience.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Replace with a tighter list: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers unless required; **HTML5/CSS3** adds little value and dates the section.
- If accurate, add one specificity cue tied to impact, e.g. **“serverless scripting”** or **“deployment automation”** instead of just tool names.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears in Topline Skills; keep it in one place or shorten one version.
- **API integrations** and automation themes also overlap with Core Competencies and Automation & Workflow Systems; avoid repeating all three.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is useful but currently reads as a mixed tool dump rather than a focused skills line. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so it should emphasize platforms actually tied to automation/operations.

Suggested edit:
- Split automation tools from collaboration/project tools for clarity and stronger positioning.
- Rewrite as: **Automation & Workflow Systems:** Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello  
  **Collaboration Tools:** Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “built Airtable/Power Automate workflows to streamline editorial intake and cross-team publishing.”
- Consider ordering by strongest/recently used tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are generic collaboration tools, not true workflow systems; keeping them in this category weakens the section.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tools to include, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength from recent roles: enterprise email operations and audience engagement. It should signal level of use and align with the leadership shown in NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign deployment)**
- If accurate, add one qualifier to show depth: **admin/configuration**, **template management**, **list segmentation**, or **journey/campaign setup**
- Keep platform names only once; use the parenthetical to add capability rather than more tools

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo email bullets; avoid repeating newsletter scale or channel ownership here
- If Dynamics 365 was only limited exposure, move it later in the list or remove it to keep the section credible

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content ownership, and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support daily web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or team/process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce stacked clauses: split team-building, website work, content production, and supervision into distinct points.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if kept there, use different emphasis here (e.g., launched/produced early series).
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; specify what changed or cut it.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy teams.”
- Make the podcast launch the lead accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes, audience growth, stakeholder reach, or types of programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent evidence appears in later NACo positions.
